Subject: Q4 peak capacity: provisional GPU block request (AuroraTech)

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for a great demo yesterday. As discussed, AuroraTech expects a Q4 production ramp starting the week of Oct 16 that will need a short runway for load testing and onboarding. High-level ask: a provisional hold on 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (or equivalent vCPU/GPU mix) across two availability zones for a 60–90 day runway while contracts finalize.

Attached is our pared-down capacity workbook with the expected token throughput and preferred AZ split. Can your team confirm the requested hold window and whether you need a formal SOW/PO before we place a provisional block?

Key dates:
- Desired hold start: 2028-10-01
- Initial throughput tests: Oct 16–23
- Production go-live target: Nov 6

Next step: If you confirm the runway, I’ll route an internal hold request to Ops and Legal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-11T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Q4 peak capacity: provisional GPU block request (AuroraTech)

Team —

Forwarding Samir's note. They want a provisional hold on 24 A100-equivalent GPUs across two AZs, target start 2028-10-01. They said they can sign quickly once they see the SOW.

Request: can Ops place a temporary block (soft or provisional) that prevents other sales from committing these specific nodes while we move contracts? If we can set a short window (21–30 days) that would materially de-risk the deal.

Considerations:
- This is a late-stage opportunity with likely expansion if PoC goes well (Aurora is a high-revenue, strategic prospect).
- We should avoid cascading conflicts with the Orion pipeline (Rishi flagged another possible ramp in mid-Oct).

Please advise on what form of hold is possible (soft block, hard reservation, buffer enforcement) and the operational checklist so I can set expectations with Samir.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-11T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Q4 peak capacity: provisional GPU block request (AuroraTech)

Marissa —

Inventory snapshot and options below. Attached: inventory_snapshot_0908.pdf and late_stage_hold_template.docx for legal ops.

Current usable headroom (across US-west clusters):
- Cluster A (us-west-1a): 40 A100-eq GPUs (20 free, 20 reserved for scheduled ramps)
- Cluster B (us-west-1b): 32 A100-eq GPUs (10 free, 22 in rolling maintenance window)

Options to satisfy a 24-GPU provisional hold:
1) Soft block (recommended immediate): place a 21-day soft hold on 24 GPUs spread 12/12 across A/B. This prevents new sales commits but allows Ops to reassign in a SEV with exec approval.
2) Hard reserve (requires manager approval & revenue commit): convert 24 GPUs to a dedicated pool, impacts capacity for the next 60 days.
3) Cross-region mitigation: we can split 12 GPUs in us-west and 12 in us-east to avoid conflict with Orion (but would change egress profile and likely pricing).

Risk: Orion's ramp (mid-Oct) may require 16 GPUs in us-west — if we do a hard reserve for Aurora in us-west we block Orion and will need exec tradeoff.

Recommendation: approve a 21-day soft block now and start paperwork. If Aurora signs a 3-month commit in the SOW, convert to a hard reserve and adjust quotas; that gives us both runway and operational flexibility.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-11T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Q4 peak capacity: provisional GPU block request (AuroraTech)

Filing a quick note on pricing and approvals. If we go soft-block -> hard reserve on signature, finance needs a 10% buffer on the quoted commit to cover egress/burst variability. That buffer can be applied as an explicit line item or absorbed into a committed usage tier.

Ask for leadership: approval to place a 21-day provisional soft block now (no revenue impact) and proceed to send the SOW. If Aurora signs within the 21 days we authorize conversion to a hard reserve and run the pricing buffer by Finance.

Lauren — can you confirm we have authority to approve a 21-day soft block without escalating to VP?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroratech.com>, Kate O'Neill <kate.oneill@auroratech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-12T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 peak capacity: provisional GPU block request (AuroraTech)

Samir / Kate —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Ops and Sales Ops guidance we will place a 21-day provisional soft block for 24 A100-equivalent GPUs starting today (2028-09-12). This prevents new sales commits to those specific nodes while allowing emergency reassignments with exec sign-off.

What happens next:
- You will receive a short SOW and provisional hold notice (attached) within 4 business hours.
- If Aurora signs a 3-month commit as discussed, we will convert the soft block to a hard reserve and finalize pricing (Karthik / Finance will share buffer options).
- Please review the attached provisional_hold_notice.pdf and confirm any AZ preferences (we've tentatively split 12/12 across us-west-1a/us-west-1b).

We’ll schedule a 30-minute ops sync this week to confirm networking and test windows. Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/sales/auroratech-hold (tentative).

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
